{
  "task_description": "Design the photon-detection system for the far detector of a liquid-argon neutrino experiment. Modules are inaccessible once the cryostat is filled. Use the simulation and the project documents to choose the module design and the wall coverage.",
  "goal": "Achieve the highest possible light collection (photoelectrons per MeV).",
  "constraints": [
    "The module must be one of the three designs listed in candidate_specs.md.",
    "At most 5% of modules may fail after 20 thermal cycles (300 K to 87 K). This is a hard requirement, because failed modules cannot be replaced.",
    "Wall coverage between 5% and 30%.",
    "Finish by submitting one recommended module design and coverage."
  ]
}

# Candidate module designs
- Module-D1: large-area light guide with thin bonded dichroic filter.
- Module-D2: wavelength-shifting bar with SiPM readout.
- Module-D3: compact SiPM tile array.

# Earlier simulation summary (2025, 20% coverage)
Light collection: Module-D1 38 PE/MeV, Module-D2 27 PE/MeV, Module-D3 18 PE/MeV. It rises with coverage, roughly as coverage^0.8.

# Thermal-cycling tests
Batches of 40 modules of each design were cycled 20 times between 300 K and 87 K.
Fraction failed (open channels or delamination):
- Module-D1: 30%  (the thin light-guide bonding cracks on cooldown)
- Module-D2: 2%
- Module-D3: 0.5%
Requirement: at most 5% failures after 20 cycles.

# Meeting notes 2026-01-20
Cabling feedthroughs were reviewed; enough feedthroughs are available for up to 30% coverage.

# Cryostat
Membrane cryostat; argon purity better than 100 ppt O2-equivalent is expected after recirculation.

# Cold electronics
The cold amplifiers have been validated for every candidate module design.

input.justification: D1 has the highest light yield but fails thermal cycling at 30%, against a 5% limit. That is a hard requirement because modules can't be replaced. D2 passes at 2% failures and has higher yield than D3 (27 vs 18 PE/MeV at 20% coverage). Yield rises with coverage, and feedthroughs support up to 30%. So I chose D2 at 30% coverage. The estimate of about 37 PE/MeV comes from extrapolating the 2025 simulation with the roughly coverage^0.8 scaling. I didn't simulate it directly at 30%. The thermal test used 40 modules per design, so the 2% figure rests on a small sample (about 1 failure).

requirements.evidence: D2 at 30% coverage is estimated at about 37 PE/MeV (27*(30/20)^0.8). This is the best yield among designs that pass the thermal requirement. The figure is an extrapolation.
D2 failed 2% in both the test document and the query. The batch was only 40 modules, so the uncertainty is large.

requirements.evidence: 30% coverage. The feedthrough review confirms capacity for up to 30%.
